heading: 7.1 Unit names as field types
text:
### 7.1 Unit names as field types [LUNI.7.1]

Any declared unit symbol is a valid field type, alongside the primitive types
(`Int`, `String`, `Bool`, …) and `Float`. The compiler resolves the unit to
its dimension, storage type, and conversion parameters.

A declared dimension name ([LUNI.4.1]) or scalar-group name ([LUNI.4.2]) is a
valid field type too. Such a slot is typed by its dimension and names no unit.
It holds its value in the dimension's base unit and storage type ([LUNI.7.2]),
so a value of the same dimension written to it is converted to the base unit,
and the rules of [LUNI.8] apply to it as to any unit-typed slot.

A dimension name is a type only for a slot and for a service kwarg
([LGRA.23.2]). It names no unit, so no unit literal is written with it, and a
`let` or `const` annotation refuses it ([LUNI.8.6], [LGRA.4.1]).

`Float` still works for untyped fields. Migration from `Float` to a unit type is
gradual and author-driven.
